content.text: The cluster-side picture is clear from the pod logs, and the root cause is outside Kubernetes (Kafka broker-side throttling and partition count). Let me resolve with a specific action for the owner.

input.note:
Cause: the ingest pods are healthy (all Running/Ready, low CPU, no restarts), so the backlog is not a Kubernetes-side problem. Two independent issues on the Kafka side are visible in the producer logs of clickstream-ingest-6f9d8c7b4-2kqvx:

1) Broker is throttling the producer on the client API key. Logs show repeated librdkafka THROTTLE warnings from multiple brokers (b0/b2/b5 of pkc-4r297.us-east-1.aws.confluent.cloud) with throttle windows of ~2.7–3.0s, and the stats line reports "producer queue=96% full, avg produce throttle_time=2.8s". With compression (zstd) and batching already enabled, the client has no more headroom — this is a broker-enforced producer bandwidth/quota cap on the API key.

2) The source topic clickstream-raw has only 4 partitions. The consumer log line "assigned partitions [0,1,2,3] (8 members in group clickstream-ingest)" shows that after scaling from 4 to 8 replicas, 4 pods have no partitions assigned and sit idle. That is why scaling the Deployment from 4→8 did not change the drain rate — a Kafka consumer group cannot have more active consumers than partitions.

Fix (owner action):
 - Scale the Deployment back to 4 replicas; the extra 4 pods cannot help until clickstream-raw has more partitions.
 - File a request with the data platform team to (a) raise the producer bandwidth quota on this API key (produce throttle is the current bottleneck, confirmed by broker THROTTLE messages and the ~96% full producer queue), and (b) increase the partition count of clickstream-raw so this service can be horizontally scaled past 4 consumers. Once partitions are increased, scale replicas up to at most the new partition count.
 - No Kubernetes-side change (resources, HPA, image) will help; CPU is ~0.11 cores per pod and pods are not resource-constrained.
